# Literature survey, evidence class E3 (generated by experiments/survey_literature.py)

Reports: 214375 (CTD-curated 5191, PubTator3-associate 70088, PubTator3-cause 39199, PubTator3-inhibit 3492, PubTator3-stimulate 6277, PubTator3-treat 90128) over 134747 papers and 22275 (perturbation, symptom, relation) triples. Document metadata (species, publication types) was fetched for 32647 of 134747 papers (cap --max-pmids 30000, papers with a directional relation first); 102100 papers have no metadata, so the 159342 reports on them carry the design metadata_not_fetched by construction, distinct from not_reported (metadata read, no design inferable). Literature reports are grade E soft priors: under the design they would enter training only for training-fold perturbations and never as evaluation positives; in the current build the experiment loader keeps grades A and B as labels and refuses D and E, so literature rows enter the report table and the reliability fit only, and the fold-aware exclusion is the rule to implement when the soft prior is wired into training.

A directional statement (cause, treat, prevent, stimulate, inhibit, marker/mechanism, therapeutic) on the mixed-polarity descriptor Bipolar Disorder D001714 is recorded as associated_with, because the diagnosis has the opposite mood pole as a cardinal feature and a treat or cause relation on it carries no sign for mania. Depressed mood has no symptom-level channel in PubTator3 or CTD (Depression D003863 is outside their disease vocabulary), so every depressed_mood report is diagnosis-level.

## Rubric weights

Quantiles (0.1: 0.210, 0.25: 0.210, 0.5: 0.245, 0.75: 0.300, 0.9: 0.420). Weights: randomised trial 1.0, cohort or case-control 0.9, genetic association 0.8, case report 0.6, animal 0.5, review or secondary 0.4, not reported (metadata read, no design inferable) 0.35, metadata not fetched 0.3; times 0.7 for a diagnosis-level descriptor. Species decide before publication types: a paper whose only annotated species is non-human is an animal study whatever its publication types.
